title: Onramp SLA fit, GPU classification, and phased scale plan for Dedicated enterprise intake
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a deterministic intake and triage flow for enterprise Dedicated capacity requests that maps customer SLA targets (latency, availability, reserved throughput) to a recommended GPU class and a phased scaling policy. The goal is to reduce back-and-forth with sales/solutions, cut onboarding time by 40%, and ensure we capture risk vectors (multi-region, preemption tolerance, RLHF/streaming workloads). Deliverables: intake scoring sheet, GPU-fit decision matrix, sample contract SLO language, and an operational phased scale plan (onboarding -> steady state -> burst).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form scored end-to-end with fields to calculate a priority score (latency SLA, tokens/sec, burst ratio, regional resilience, data residency)
GPU-fit decision matrix that maps workload archetypes to recommended GPU families (H100, A100, L4) with rationale and cost multiplier estimates
Phased scale plan template (3 phases) that ops can consume: initial reserve, auto-scale triggers, burst credit policy, and preemptible fallback rules
Legal/contract sample with clear SLA targets and measurement windows for 99.9% availability and P95 latency where applicable
Pilot run with 2 enterprise customers (one LLM-streaming-heavy, one high-throughput embedding) documented with outcomes and runbook updates

notes: Trade-offs discussed: recommending H100 increases unit cost by ~2.3x over L4 but reduces latency tail and provides larger memory for KV cache. For many embedding-heavy customers, L4 + aggressive batching is more cost-effective.
Risk: customers using customer-managed VPCs may require longer onboarding windows; plan adds a +2 week buffer to timeline for Private deployments.
Operational constraint: autoscale ramping should be capped to avoid noisy neighbor impact; propose per-customer max ramp per 10m window (to be validated by ENG).

Fallback strategy options: (A) degrade model family (H100->A100->L4), (B) throttle requests with queued backpressure, (C) route lower-priority traffic to shared-hosted tier. Recommendation: combine A+B for predictable behavior.
